Naming that same\napplication explicitly is the identical operation and is treated as such.\nOnly postgres and mariadb accept a different target.","type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"type":"string","enum":["","postgres","mariadb","instance","disk"],"description":"Kind of the application: postgres, mariadb, instance (VM instance) or disk (VM disk). Empty in a response only for an application of a kind with no backup driver, which can exist only if created outside this API."},"name":{"type":"string"}}},"confirmDestructive":{"type":"boolean","description":"Required whenever the resolved target is the source application, or is an existing application that already holds data."},"recoveryTime":{"type":"string","format":"date-time","description":"Postgres only. Must fall inside the backup's recovery_window: at or after\nearliest, before last_commit_at and before cross_timeline_after. Omit it to\nrestore the state restore_point names. Exclusive with restore_point latest."},"originalDisks":{"type":"string","enum":["","discard","keep"],"description":"What becomes of the disks a VM instance restored over its source displaces. Either way they are replaced by the backup's copies. discard, the default, which empty means: what they held is deleted once the restore has succeeded, so a restore that says nothing does not start paying for a second copy; a restore that fails or is cancelled deletes nothing and keeps them as keep does, and its message says so. keep: what they held is kept as a disk of its own, named <disk>-orig-<id>, attached to nothing, listed and billed like any other disk. keep is refused on any other restore."},"restorePoint":{"type":"string","enum":["","backup","latest"],"description":"Postgres only, and only without recovery_time. backup, the default, which empty means: the state of the backup named. latest: the latest state its archived log reaches, along its history."}}}}},"required":true}}
>
